facts.text: I've been having episodes where I get confused.
During these episodes I get shaky.

facts.item: how often the episodes have happened
facts.text: I've had several of these episodes over the past week.
They come in the morning and in the evening, after I've gone several hours without eating.
They go away when I eat something with sugar in it.

facts.item: finger-stick sugar readings during the episodes
facts.text: When the sugar was checked with a finger-stick meter during the episodes, the readings were in the 30s.
I have a myoepithelial carcinoma of my left parotid (salivary) gland, and it has spread.
I'm having chemotherapy infusions; I came in today for a routine one.
I took metformin for my diabetes until recently; it was stopped after the low sugars began.
I take levothyroxine for my thyroid.

findings.name: serum glucose
findings.result: 30 mg/dL before the chemotherapy infusion; 33 mg/dL during a later episode in hospital.

findings.name: finger-stick glucose readings at home
findings.result: Values in the 30s during the episodes.

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Liver enzymes stably elevated; bilirubin normal; albumin mildly decreased.

findings.name: serum insulin
findings.result: <1 μU/mL (reference 3–25), drawn while glucose was 33 mg/dL.

findings.name: C-peptide
findings.result: <0.5 ng/mL (reference 1.1–4.3), drawn while glucose was 33 mg/dL.

findings.name: β-hydroxybutyrate
findings.result: <1.0 mmol/L (reference <3), drawn while glucose was 33 mg/dL.

findings.name: serum cortisol
findings.result: Random cortisol 23 μg/dL (reference morning 8–25), drawn while glucose was 33 mg/dL.

findings.name: insulin-like growth factors
findings.result: IGF-1 15 ng/mL (reference 41–279); IGF-2 147 ng/mL (reference 180–580); IGF-2:IGF-1 molar ratio 10.

gold.reasoning: 1. Medication‐induced hypoglycemia was considered and ruled out — “after medication-induced hypoglycemia and insulinoma have been excluded.” 2. Insulinoma was considered unlikely given suppressed insulin and C-peptide — “the patient’s low insulin, C-peptide, and β-hydroxybutyrate levels during an episode of hypoglycemia indicated a noninsulin mediated process.” 3. Impaired gluconeogenesis from liver metastases was considered but deemed unlikely because synthetic liver function remained intact — “this was felt to be unlikely as the patient’s liver synthetic function was intact.”

x002: Home or outpatient readings before the index visit; the meter values are approximate ('in the 30s').
x011: IGF-1 and IGF-2 are kept together because the reported molar ratio needs both values.

source_issues: The INR is described only as normal, and the liver enzymes only as 'stably elevated', without values.
notes: Index visit: the routine chemotherapy visit at which the pre-infusion glucose was 30 mg/dL, leading to admission (s001-s006); the episodes of the preceding week are history.
'Fulfilling Whipple's triad' (s002) is the clinician's interpretation and is not part of any fact.
s005: the levothyroxine dose increase is treatment during the admission and is not used; the patient's levothyroxine use (implied by the dose change and her hypothyroidism) is a medication fact.
